content: This paper introduces a new approach to estimate preference polarization in multidimensional settings using texts and votes. First, a distributional representation of textual data is utilized to retain qualities of human speech that are otherwise discarded by a bag-of-words approach. Second, community detection in multiplex networks is used to uncover preference affinity blocs across multiple layers of votes and speeches. Just as scaling and spatial models attempt to explain variance along one or a few reduced dimensions, our approach identifies densely connected communities based on preference similarity that are important for explaining variations in observed outcomes.
